title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compared a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the preregistered confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate per pair) all confirmatory episodes completed: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (i) publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints needed to reproduce the run, (ii) diagnose—using the archived artifacts—why the paired outcome is uninformative about independent generative reliability (shared_initial_candidate design, template‑tight task synthesis, and validator–task coupling), and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable experimental modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversity, task heterogeneity) that produce informative independent comparisons. The immutable initial master prompt is archived (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps via natural‑language intent → device configuration mapping is an active area of research and deployment. Generative LLMs promise reduced operator effort and rapid provisioning, but semantic correctness—reachability, access‑control preservation, ordering and transient safety—is safety‑critical. Prior work demonstrates the value of verifier grounding and generate–validate–repair pipelines for operational correctness (e.g., Batfish evolution and verifier‑based NetOps tooling [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]).

We preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment to answer a single, clearly stated question: in a verifier‑grounded paired design, does a single‑pass LLM generator produce a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline on a programmatic set of synthetic intent→configuration tasks? The preregistered plan and all artifacts were frozen before execution (see preregistration SHA‑256 above and execution manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). The study was intentionally constrained to enable deterministic auditing: (1) tasks were synthesizeable from deterministic templates with explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies (task_manifest.jsonl), (2) the validator was deterministic and archived (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and (3) all provider calls, responses, scoring artifacts and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes were archived and published in the execution bundle.

This paper (a) reports the preregistered confirmatory run and exact quantitative outcomes, (b) documents the complete artifact set and reproduction pointers with SHA‑256 fingerprints, (c) provides an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of the degenerate paired outcome, and (d) gives concrete, runnable changes for informative follow‑ups. We do not invent additional experiments or data: all quantitative numbers and file identifiers below are taken verbatim from the archived execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Verifier‑grounded NetOps research and tools demonstrate how high‑fidelity validators improve pre‑deployment correctness and reduce outages; Batfish is a canonical example and its evolution highlights the operational benefits of deterministic analysis for configuration correctness [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps studies focus on intent translation, template synthesis, or generate–validate repair loops; many emphasize that token‑level metrics misrepresent semantic correctness and advocate verifier‑centric evaluation [https://doi.org/10.23919/cnsm62983.2024.10814407, https://doi.org/10.1002/nem.70029].

Our contribution is orthogonal: rather than introduce a new model or dataset, we preregister and publish a fully archived confirmatory execution whose design, execution log, per‑episode validator traces, and statistical analysis are all reproducible via the provided artifact bundle. The experiment illustrates how confirmatory semantics (shared candidate vs. independent sampling) materially change the interpretation of paired verifier comparisons and how artifact release enables immediate audit and surgical reruns.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The frozen preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) specified a paired confirmatory test (H1): the estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline across N = 120 programmatic tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS). The primary analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1 using 10,000 bootstrap resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) for CI estimation. Secondary, exploratory analyses (seed sensitivity, rank stability) were predeclared for post‑hoc investigation.

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were generated deterministically from an intent template bank (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, generator_version 5.0). Each task payload contains: (i) initial_state and expected_final_state, (ii) required_sequence (the canonical command sequence satisfying the intent), (iii) per‑task workflow_policies (e.g., "must_be_down_for_fields", minimum_active_in_groups), and (iv) allowed_touched_fields. Representative task manifest entries are archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl. The preregistration enforced inclusion/exclusion rules: any task whose gold template failed unit tests (parse or baseline verifier) was to be excluded and replaced so that N = 120 confirmatory pairs would remain.

Generation semantics and confirmatory design choice. The preregistered confirmatory generation_semantics was set to "shared_initial_candidate": for each pair the pipeline produced a single canonical candidate (seed_0) and supplied that identical candidate to both the deterministic template baseline and the guarded (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluation episodes. This design isolates any scoring pipeline or validator condition differences but does not capture independent generative variability across conditions. The choice and its practical consequence are central to our subsequent diagnosis; the immutable provider call traces and shared candidate files are archived (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt and execution/provider_calls/*-shared-initial.json).

Models, adapter, and validator. Declared LLM: gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; the model configuration is archived (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The deterministic validator is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0); scoring rule used: full_intent_constraint_validation. Per‑episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task‑NNN‑<condition>.json) record normalized_response, validator_trace (validation_before/after), parsed_command_count, and the binary score. All scoring artifacts are published and hashed.

Execution accounting and reproducibility controls. Planned_episode_count = 240 (2 episodes per pair). Execution started 2026‑08‑27T14:49:02.808900+00:00 and completed 2026‑08‑27T15:04:49.334056+00:00 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120; failed_episode_count = 0. The execution bundle includes a full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest (execution/*). A contamination detection procedure (exact‑match and normalized 5‑gram overlap thresholds) was applied and its report archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv).
sections.results:
Execution and raw outcomes. All confirmatory episodes completed without infrastructure failures: complete_pair_count = 120; baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. The paired contingency table is degenerate: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 9f25790c7e...). The primary estimator (mean over tasks of guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00.

Statistical inference. We followed the preregistered analysis: bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) for the paired difference produced a 95% CI [0.00, 0.00] (analysis log: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). McNemar exact two‑sided test yields p = 1.0 (degenerate because there are zero discordant pairs). All numeric results and the raw scoring JSONs referenced below match the archived artifacts exactly.

Representative per‑task evidence. Example pair pair‑000001 (task‑000001): shared_initial candidate (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...) is identical to both the baseline and guarded responses; the scoring JSON is execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). The validator_trace in that scoring JSON shows parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, violation_count = 0 and validator final_state matching the expected_final_state. Similar identicalities appear in many pairs (examples: task‑000002, task‑000003 with respective shared_initial artifacts and scoring JSONs). The provider call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 120 and cache_miss_count = 120 (deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Contamination and quality checks. The preregistered contamination heuristics found no confirmatory flags under pre‑specified thresholds; the contamination summary is archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0d1e8...). All execution hashes for key artifacts are present in the execution manifest; representative file SHA‑256s cited here allow exact verification without re‑execution.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded diagnosis of degeneracy. The degenerate confirmatory outcome is fully explicable from archived design choices and task structure: (1) shared_initial_candidate semantics—seed_0 produced a single canonical candidate per pair which was used for both baseline and guarded episodes (evidence: execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt and execution/provider_calls/*-shared-initial.json), (2) templated task synthesis—each task payload encoded a deterministic required_sequence tightly aligned with validator constraints (evidence: execution/task_manifest.jsonl entries contain required_sequence and workflow_policies), and (3) validator–task coupling—the deterministic validator enforces task template constraints (deterministic_netops_validator_v5 traces in execution/scoring/*.json). Together these cause identical canonical candidates to validate under both conditions, producing n_11 = N.

Implication for confirmatory design. A confirmatory paired test that reuses identical per‑pair candidates measures whether the validator treats identical artifacts differently across conditions; it does not measure independent model reliability under operational sampling. To evaluate independent generative robustness the confirmatory semantics must supply independent candidates per condition (independent_per_condition) or use multiple confirmatory seeds per condition as predeclared exploratory replicates.

Runnable corrective modifications (artifact‑grounded). The following changes are implementable using the released bundle and will yield informative, independent comparisons: (A) independent_per_condition confirmatory sampling: modify the generation stage to produce one candidate per condition per pair and re‑run the pipeline (edit execution/adapter config and re‑use execution/task_manifest.jsonl); (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design: treat seeds_0..K as confirmatory replicates and compute within‑condition pass probabilities before paired contrasts; (C) validator diversity: add a second validator (e.g., reachability/emulation or Batfish‑style analyzer) and report intersection/union pass rates to reduce task–validator coupling; (D) task heterogeneity: expand template bank with paraphrase variants and randomized constraint perturbations to broaden constructive validity. All of these changes are operationally supported by the archived code and task manifest; exact paths for reruns and hashes are published in execution/execution_manifest.json.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the preregistered shared_initial design intentionally constrained variability and therefore reduces the internal evidential scope for independent generative claims. Construct validity: deterministic validators enforce template constraints and may not represent open operational distributions. External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency table yields trivial inferential statistics that are arithmetically correct but substantively uninformative about independent generative reliability.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and published the complete execution and analysis artifact bundle. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate confirmatory semantics (explicit in the frozen plan) both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on the 120 synthetic tasks (both 120/120). Artifact evidence (shared_initial candidate files and scoring JSONs) shows the proximate cause: identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight tasks coupled to a deterministic validator. Consequently the observed perfect agreement does not establish independent LLM reliability in realistic operational distributions. We release the full artifact bundle (execution/*, analysis/*, deterministic_reconciliation.json, provenance/master_prompt.txt) including per‑file SHA‑256 hashes so others can (i) reproduce the exact run, (ii) reconfigure generation semantics to independent_per_condition or multi‑seed confirmatory designs, and (iii) re‑execute with validator diversification and more heterogeneous templates to obtain informative independent comparisons. A brief, high‑visibility caution: because the preregistered confirmatory semantics used identical per‑pair candidates, the confirmatory paired test does not evaluate independent model generative robustness—this statement is supported by the archived artifacts and hashes cited in the Disclosure and above. The provided bundle contains the exact artifacts (paths and SHA‑256s) required to reproduce and to rerun the variants recommended above, enabling immediate audit and follow‑up experiments for operationally informative evaluation of LLM‑driven NetOps automation.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
